characterization_methods.key_findings: YS ≈350–450 MPa; UTS at a minimum near 2Al; TE collapses at 2Al for the 550 °C, 24 h condition (Fig. 3).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature, initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; values are averages of three measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)

characterization_methods.key_findings: ≈200 HBW for the 2Al alloy (flat ~200 HBW over 0–6 Al).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm

characterization_methods.key_findings: no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations; recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction by grinding and polishing with standard metallographic techniques
characterization_methods.purpose: detect cracks, pores, macrosegregations and characterize microstructure

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five Cu molds moved stepwise inside the furnace, successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into segments with dimensions 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ for each alloy composition.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Averages of three measurements for every material state

hardness.uncertainty: approximate; hardness nearly flat around 200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al

yield_strength.uncertainty: approximate; read from Fig. 3a (YS stays between roughly the 350 and 450 MPa lines from 0Al to 4Al for the 550 °C, 24 h curve)

structures.overall_structure: Single-phase austenitic (SIMPLEX TWIP) steel; fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 μm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations; metallographic analysis showed no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations.

unmapped_findings: The Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al alloy is an intermediate-Al variant: its mechanical data fall between the Al-free alloy (weakening/embrittlement on aging) and the Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al alloy (strengthening on aging), with a much smaller influence of aging on tensile behavior in the 2–6 wt.% Al cases (b0024, b0025).

In Fig. 3b the 550 °C, 24 h (green) UTS curve reaches a minimum near 2Al (annotated '550 °C, 24h'), and Fig. 3c shows total elongation collapses at 2Al for the 550 °C, 24 h condition; no numeric UTS/TE values are printed for the 2Al data point (figure_003).

In Fig. 4 the 2Al (pale cyan) data cluster at roughly 460–600 MPa tensile strength with elongation spanning ~8% to ~55%, but this range covers the 2Al alloy across all tested aging conditions (450/500/550/600 °C, 1 h and 24 h) and is not specific to the 550 °C, 24 h condition (figure_004).

κ-carbide nanoprecipitates (L′1₂, approximate stoichiometry (Fe,Mn)₃AlC) form upon aging in Al-containing alloys; however, for the 2–6 wt.% Al intermediate alloys no equivalent κ-carbide strengthening is reported, so significant κ-carbide formation in this 2Al/550 °C-24 h sample is not explicitly confirmed (b0015, b0025).

This sample falls within the SIMPLEX/TWIP composition range (25–30 wt.% Mn, up to 4–5 wt.% Al), so mechanical twinning/dislocation-based strain hardening is the expected prevailing deformation mechanism rather than pronounced κ-carbide strengthening (b0031).
